headline: Mensah takes over QB1; Sayin and Lacy injuries shake up the top
detail: Stats now run through Saturday 10/24. The QB order changed the most: Darian Mensah is QB1 on most late-October boards (Draft Countdown, WalterFootball, NFL Draft Buzz, Dynasty Nerds), Manning slipped after a rough stretch, and Julian Sayin's throwing-shoulder injury (10/17) leaves him out indefinitely. Four receivers and tight ends were added off multiple boards, and three fringe WRs were cut to keep each position at 35. This week also adds the overall Top 35, built for your league (2 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE, 3 flex, PPR), so QBs rank higher than on a standard 1-QB board.

headline: How the board moves each week
detail: Each Monday the position ranks are re-blended from the newest NFL draft big boards and dynasty rookie rankings. This week used DraftTek 10/21, Draft Countdown 10/22, TheBigBoard.gg 10/25, WalterFootball 10/20, PFF stock up/down 10/19, Kiper via B/R 10/15 and Dynasty Nerds 10/14. Players move when several boards agree, or when injuries, production or declare news change their outlook. A player with no new board info keeps his place relative to his neighbors, so he can slip a spot or two only because others moved around him. The overall Top 35 never reorders players within a position; it decides how positions interleave for your 2-QB PPR format.

headline: Mestemaker retakes QB1; Sellers and Alexander climb; two new names
detail: Stats now run through Saturday 10/31. Mel Kiper's 10/30 board drove most moves: Drew Mestemaker is back at QB1 over Darian Mensah, Austin Simmons jumps to QB6, and Deuce Alexander rises to WR6. LaNorris Sellers had the best week, with 301 passing and 96 rushing yards in a win at Oklahoma, and moves to QB7. Injuries took Kewan Lacy, Kamari Moulton and Dante Moore's outlooks down: Moore and Moulton are reported out for the year and Lacy may be. Jackson Harris (LSU) and Kendrick Raphael (SMU) are added; T.J. Moore and Bryant Wesco Jr. slip out of the Top 35.

headline: Carr up to QB3; Jackson Harris, Roberts and Thurman climb; three added
detail: Stats now run through Saturday 11/7. CJ Carr beat No. 1 Miami with 319 yds and 3 TD and Kiper's 11/5 board moved him to No. 8, so he passes Trinidad Chambliss (170 yds, 0 TD in a 42-7 loss to Georgia) at QB3. Jackson Harris (11-166 vs Alabama, Kiper's new WR5), Jamal Roberts (RB6, into the Top 35), Mark Fletcher Jr. (Kiper's RB2) and Jelani Thurman (Kiper's TE4) are the big risers. Season-ending injuries drop Hollywood Smothers (torn MCL), Duce Robinson (torn ACL) and Peter Clarke (broken fibula). Gio Lopez, Devin McCuin and Patrick Overmyer are added; Anthony Evans III is cut for the WR cap.

headline: Top 35 re-ranked for superflex; 10-team mock draft added
detail: The overall Top 35 now fits your actual league: superflex PPR with QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, TE, 2 flex and no TE premium. It was built for a 2-QB lineup before. QBs still go early, but a little less so, and receivers gain because you start three. The new Mock draft tab projects a 10-team, 4-round rookie draft from 18 superflex and 1QB mocks and rankings published since late August. Big swing names: Arch Manning (anywhere from 2 to 29 depending on whether he returns to Texas), Julian Sayin (3 to 52), Nate Frazier (6 to 42). Dante Moore isn't expected back this season, so the newest mocks have him in the late teens.

headline: How the mock draft is built
detail: Start from the superflex consensus (average draft slot across fall 2026 mocks and rankings, with a missing player counted as below the list), then adjust for this league: 10 teams instead of 12, TEs moved back because most published mocks use TE premium, and players with real return-to-school or injury risk (Manning, Sayin, Hardy, Simmons) priced lower. The Top 35 uses the same market order but keeps each position in our position-rank order.
